pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: crates/apps/extractor/src/lib.rs:1300 Extractor's params schema is published as an agent tool inputSchema (registry::tool_definition) and enforced at the enqueue door. It encodes mode-dependent requiredness as oneOf branches. A conflicting call is therefore refused with jsonschema's generic 'not valid under any of the oneOf schemas' text. The diagnosable message that names the conflicts comes from resolve_run_mode, which the door never reaches.

techniques.evidence: crates/apps/extractor/src/lib.rs:1300 Requiredness that varies by operation (mode) sits in the schema instead of a uniform runtime rule. The door error (validate_params formats the raw jsonschema errors) cannot say which mode moved the requirement.
crates/apps/extractor/tests/mode_door.rs:84 The test proves the published schema and the app's own guard refuse the same objects, using the real validator crate.

pairs.registryProposal: tool-schema-design's conditional-requiredness rule assumes a flat schema cannot express operation-dependent requiredness. It could say explicitly whether oneOf/if-then branches count as 'in the schema', given that their validator errors are the undiagnosable kind the rule warns against.
